title: Resetting Your Password
content: If you've forgotten your password, click 'Forgot Password' on the login screen and enter your account email. You'll receive a reset link valid for 30 minutes. For security, TicketOps never sends your password directly - you'll always set a new one via this link.

title: Enabling Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
content: Two-factor authentication adds an extra layer of security to your account. Go to Account Settings > Security > Enable 2FA, then scan the QR code with an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy. Once enabled, you'll need a 6-digit code at every login.

title: Single Sign-On (SSO) for Teams
content: TicketOps supports SAML-based Single Sign-On for teams on the Business and Enterprise plans. Your admin can configure SSO under Team Settings > Security > SSO Configuration, connecting to identity providers like Okta, Azure AD, or Google Workspace.

title: Understanding Your Subscription Plans
content: TicketOps offers three plans: Basic (up to 3 seats, core ticketing features), Pro (up to 15 seats, automation rules and reporting), and Business (unlimited seats, SSO, and priority support). All plans are billed monthly or annually, with a 15% discount for annual billing.

title: How Refunds Work
content: If you're on a monthly plan and cancel within 7 days of your billing date, you're eligible for a full refund of that month's charge. Annual plans are refundable on a prorated basis only within the first 30 days of the annual term. Refund requests are processed within 5-7 business days.

title: Cancelling Your Subscription
content: You can cancel anytime from Account Settings > Billing > Cancel Subscription. Your account remains active until the end of the current billing period. After cancellation, your data is retained for 90 days in case you want to reactivate, after which it is permanently deleted.

title: Understanding Your Invoice
content: Each invoice breaks down your base plan cost, any add-on seats, and applicable taxes. A 'proration adjustment' line item appears if you changed plans mid-cycle. If you see a charge you don't recognize, contact billing support with your invoice number.

title: Data Export to CSV
content: You can export your tickets, contacts, and reports to CSV at any time from the Reports tab by clicking 'Export'. Exports include all fields visible in your current filtered view, and large exports (over 10,000 rows) are emailed to you as a download link instead of downloading directly.

title: Automating Recurring Reports
content: Automation Rules let you schedule recurring actions, including automatically exporting a report on a daily, weekly, or monthly cadence and emailing it to a chosen recipient list. Set this up under Automation > New Rule > Trigger: Schedule.

title: Slack Integration
content: Connect TicketOps to Slack under Integrations > Slack to receive real-time notifications for new tickets, mentions, and SLA breaches directly in a channel of your choice. You can customize which event types are sent to Slack in the integration settings.

title: Zapier Integration
content: TicketOps connects to over 3,000 apps via Zapier, letting you trigger actions like creating a ticket from a form submission or updating a CRM record when a ticket is resolved. Find our Zapier app by searching 'TicketOps' in your Zapier account.

title: API Access and Rate Limits
content: The TicketOps REST API is available on Pro and Business plans. API requests are rate-limited to 100 requests per minute per API key on Pro, and 500 requests per minute on Business. Exceeding the limit returns a 429 status code with a Retry-After header.

title: Generating an API Key
content: API keys are created under Account Settings > Developer > API Keys. Each key can be scoped to read-only or read-write access. Keep your API key secret - if it's ever exposed, revoke it immediately and generate a new one.

title: Webhooks Overview
content: Webhooks let TicketOps notify your own systems in real time when events occur, such as a ticket being created or its status changing. Configure webhook URLs under Integrations > Webhooks, and TicketOps will POST a JSON payload to your endpoint for each subscribed event.

title: Managing Team Roles and Permissions
content: TicketOps has three built-in roles: Admin (full account and billing access), Agent (can view and resolve tickets), and Viewer (read-only access to reports). Custom roles with granular permissions are available on the Business plan.

title: Adding or Removing Seats
content: Admins can add seats anytime from Account Settings > Team > Add Member, which prorates the cost for the remainder of the billing cycle. Removing a seat takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle and does not generate a refund for the current period.

title: Mobile App Overview
content: The TicketOps mobile app is available for iOS and Android and supports viewing, replying to, and reassigning tickets on the go. Push notifications can be configured under the app's Settings > Notifications, mirroring the categories available on desktop.

title: Syncing Issues Between Mobile and Desktop
content: If your mobile app isn't reflecting recent changes made on desktop, first check you're logged into the same account, then pull down to refresh the ticket list. Persistent sync issues are often resolved by logging out and back in, which forces a full resync.

title: Custom Fields
content: Custom fields let you capture ticket information specific to your business, such as 'Product SKU' or 'Renewal Date'. Create them under Settings > Custom Fields, choosing from text, number, dropdown, or date field types. Custom fields can be included in exports and reports.

title: Setting Up Automation Rules
content: Automation Rules run actions automatically when conditions are met - for example, auto-assigning tickets tagged 'billing' to your finance team, or auto-closing tickets with no customer reply after 14 days. Rules are configured under Automation > New Rule with a trigger, condition, and action.

title: Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Uptime
content: TicketOps guarantees 99.9% uptime on Business plans, with service credits issued if this is not met in a given month. Planned maintenance windows are announced at least 48 hours in advance via email and our status page.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Policy
content: Active account data is retained indefinitely while your subscription is active. After cancellation, data is kept for 90 days to allow reactivation, then permanently and irreversibly deleted from all systems, including backups, within an additional 30 days.

title: GDPR and Data Requests
content: TicketOps is GDPR compliant. EU customers can request a full export or deletion of their personal data by contacting privacy@ticketops.example. Data deletion requests are completed within 30 days as required by GDPR Article 17.

title: Account Recovery When You Can't Access Your Email
content: If you no longer have access to the email on your account, password reset links won't reach you. Contact support with proof of account ownership (such as a recent invoice) and our team will manually verify your identity before updating your account email.

title: Troubleshooting Failed Exports
content: If an export fails or gets stuck at 0%, it's usually caused by an extremely large date range or too many active filters. Try narrowing your filters or splitting the export into smaller date ranges. Exports over 10,000 rows are always sent via email link rather than direct download.

title: Contacting Support and Escalations
content: Standard support is available via email with a target response time of 24 hours on Basic and Pro plans, and 4 hours on Business plans. To escalate a critical issue, mark your ticket priority as 'Urgent' - this routes it directly to the on-call support lead.
